title: wb archive names its positional seq though under message it takes a message's anchor, where wb edit names the same positional id
body:
Filed by ic on 2026-10-23 on vc's order, from ruling (1) of 0627's spec: the positional stays `seq` in 3.2.6, and the rename to `id` is new surface behind the line, filed as its own issue.

## What

Since 0627 (37ba1be83), `intent wb archive <kind> <seq>` takes one positional for two things: an item's number within its kind, and, under `message`, a message's address, the first stamp in its inbox heading with `#<n>` to pick one of several in a minute. Its name says only the first. `intent wb edit <kind> <id> <text>` takes the same positional with the same two meanings and names it `id`, so the two verbs that address the same things spell the address differently. In 3.2.6 the positional stays `seq`, made optional (the `--handled` sweep takes none), with help text saying it is a message's anchor under `message`.

The name is surface in these places, measured at 6bd64b1c8:

- `surface/dispatch-table.json`: the `wb archive` row's second arg is `"name": "seq"`, and its help already describes both meanings. The `wb edit` row names the same arg `id`.
- The MCP arm: `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/src/mcp.rs` reads the key `seq` (lines 1372 and 1405), so an MCP client sends `seq` for a message's anchor.
- The CLI's render of the verb: `native/rust/crates/intent-cli/src/render.rs` reads `seq` (lines 4503, 4508 and 4943).
- The generated views: `docs/reference/intent-wb.md:210` prints `intent wb archive <kind> <seq> [flags]`, and `intent llm guide` prints `<seq>` in the verb's call line.
- The skill: `intent/plugins/claude/skills/in-whiteboard/SKILL.md` writes `intent wb archive <kind> <seq>` in its verb table (line 38) and in its verb notes (lines 146 and 158), beside `wb archive message <anchor> --to <node>` (line 39).

## Why it waits behind the line

Where a positional's name is a key, it is part of the contract: the MCP tool's input takes `seq`, so renaming it changes what an MCP client sends, and the guide and the command reference print it. That makes the rename new surface rather than the repair of a broken one, so it waits behind the stabilisation line drawn after 3.2.5.

## Expected

`wb archive`'s positional is named `id`, as `wb edit`'s is, with its help text unchanged in meaning. What a client still sending `seq` meets is vc's to rule when the work is specified.

## What an implementer owes

- The dispatch table's arg renamed, and the views made from it regenerated by their generators: the command reference under `docs/reference/` and `dispatch-table.md`.
- The MCP arm and the CLI render reading `id`, with one arm driving `wb archive message` over MCP with `id` and one driving `wb archive <kind> <n>` with `id`, each red at the base.
- The skill's table and notes saying `<id>`, the table re-padded and checked with prettier.
- A measurement of whether the MCP input change moves a face version, as 0627 measured its own (JSON 23 to 24), stated in the bank.
- `wb edit`'s naming is the precedent to match, not a second form to keep.
